newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - Dec 2 wk data suggest slower U.S. growth.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Dec 2 wk data suggest slower U.S. growth.

text.p: U.S. economic reports next week, including Friday's jobs data, should reflect slower economic growth in the fourth quarter, said a Reuters poll.
On average, 22 economists surveyed on Wednesday and Friday forecast non-farm payrolls grew by 179,000 in November, compared with 210,000 the month before.

A number in line with that projection would be "below the year-to-date trend," said John Park, an economist at Sanwa Securities USA Co. "It reinforces the view that there is a slowdown in the economy."
The experts also projected a 0.4 percent uptick in average hourly earnings to $11.96, as well as a tenth-of-an-hour increase in the average workweek, to 34.4 hours.

Such a wage increase would "shave a tiny bit off the twelve-months (average) rate, and it would signal no acceleration in labor costs," said Carol Stone, senior economist at Nomura Securities International Inc.

Economists said additional support for the slower-growth view should come from a decline in new home sales and non-farm productivity, and a small increase in factory orders, reports on all of which will be released next week.
A more on-the-fence number will be the National Association of Purchasing Management's November manufacturing survey, set for release on Monday, the experts said.
It will read 50.8 versus October's 50.2 if forecasters' projections are right. A reading of 50.0 indicates neutral sentiment, NAPM has said.
"That's going to be very interesting," said Stone, who forecast a low 49.6. "If our number comes to pass, I think the (bond) market rally would extend further."
